sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in North Tonawanda, NY?
sections.html:
In North Tonawanda you can list with an agent, sell on your own, or accept a direct cash purchase, and the choice usually turns on the condition of the house and how long you can wait. Start by confirming your address is inside the city, because the 14120 ZIP code also covers southern parts of the towns of Wheatfield and Pendleton.

North Tonawanda is a city of about 10.9 square miles in Niagara County, bounded by the Niagara River on the west and Tonawanda Creek and the Erie Canal on the south. The Census Bureau estimated 29,806 residents on July 1, 2025, down 2.3% from the 2020 base. It is the second-largest city in the county after Niagara Falls. Across the canal lie the City of Tonawanda and the Town of Amherst in Erie County, and the Town of Wheatfield borders North Tonawanda on the north and east.

  • Median value of an owner-occupied home, 2020 to 2024: $197,200
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 70.1%
  • Median gross rent: $934 a month
  • Median household income: $66,961
  • Residents 65 and older: 21.9%
  • Persons in poverty: 12.4%

With 14,015 households averaging 2.14 people, North Tonawanda skews toward long-time owners. About 91% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, which points to a settled owner base.

sections.h2: What is North Tonawanda known for, and who buys houses here?
sections.html:
The city calls itself the Lumber City, and its housing grew out of that history. From the mid-19th century into the 1970s it was a lumber forwarding center and, at the height of the Erie Canal, the largest port on the Great Lakes. More than 150 lumber companies operated here, and the Ray H. Bennett Lumber Company sold kit homes across the United States and Canada for about 70 years.

It is also the birthplace of the Herschell carrousel company, and the Herschell Carrousel Factory Museum is on Thompson Street. Wurlitzer took over the band organ factory in 1909, and the old Wurlitzer plant now holds light industrial and commercial tenants. Goundry Street has mansions built for lumber barons, including Kent Place at 208 Goundry Street.

The city became a village in 1865 and was incorporated as a city on April 24, 1897. Downtown draws buyers who like the Riviera Theatre on Webster Street, the City Market that opened in 1908, Gateway Harbor Park on the canal, and Gratwick-Riverside Park, a 53-acre park on the Niagara River. The arts scene downtown also includes the Ghostlight Theatre, the Carnegie Art Center in the former Carnegie Library and the Railroad Museum of the Niagara Frontier in a 1923 Erie Railroad station.

sections.h2: Do North Tonawanda rental properties have to be registered?
sections.html:
Yes. Under Chapter 51D of the city code, every owner of rental property in North Tonawanda registers each rental unit with the Building Department, and owner-occupied properties register too, without a fee.

North Tonawanda rental registration, yearly fee (City Rental Unit Registration page)
PropertyFee
1 to 3 dwelling units$35 per unit
4 or more dwelling units$140
Owner-occupiedNo fee, registration still required

A certificate is valid up to one year or until ownership changes, so the buyer of a rental house registers in their own name after the deed transfers. Registering consents to inspection by Code Enforcement for compliance with the city chapter and the New York State building and fire codes.

  • Applicants submit photo identification.
  • An owner who does not live in Niagara County, Erie, Genesee or Orleans County must name a property manager who does, and who can accept legal notices.
  • A first conviction for failing to register carries a fine of $250 to $500. A second within twelve months carries $500 to $2,500.
  • A fine unpaid after 30 days becomes a lien on the property and is collected like a tax.

If you own a rental, clear any registration gap before you sell, since a lien would surface in a title search. The Building Department number on the registration page is (716) 692-2680, and the office is at 216 Payne Avenue.

sections.h2: When can you grieve your North Tonawanda assessment?
sections.html:
Grievance Day is always the fourth Tuesday in May, and the Assessor's office has the forms starting in March. The assessor's page also carries the 2026 final roll and a property search where you can open any parcel and select Additional Info, then View Tax Detail, to see a tax summary by year.

The same office lists the exemptions a buyer may ask about:

  • Basic STAR requires owning and living in the home with 2024 income of $500,000 or less.
  • Enhanced STAR requires age 65 by the end of 2026 and 2024 adjusted gross income of $110,750 or less.
  • People who bought after 2015 sign up with the state for the STAR Credit.
  • The low-income senior exemption has a 2025 income limit of $34,400, and the disability exemption has a limit of $34,600.
  • Veterans exemptions are capped for assessments above $120,000.

The Assessor will give you a free copy of your deed on request, which helps when you are assembling closing papers. Contact the office at 695-8597 for details.

sections.h2: How are deeds filed and transfer tax paid in North Tonawanda?
sections.html:
Deeds for a North Tonawanda sale go to the Niagara County Clerk, not City Hall. The Assessor's page points filers to the clerk's deed recording office at (716) 439-7022, with recording hours of 9:30 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays.

The county clerk requires the signed original deed plus a TP-584 transfer tax return and an RP-5217 real property transfer report. The seller pays the state transfer tax of $2 for each $500, or $4 per $1,000, and the state sets the filing deadline at 15 days after the deed is delivered. A closing attorney or title company normally handles this for you.

Before closing, settle city water. The Clerk/Treasurer's office warns that after two consecutive estimated water meter readings, a $25 fee applies each quarter until the meter is read, and meter readings can be dropped off or submitted online. Ask the Treasurer's office at (716) 695-8575 for the current balance and how it is handled at transfer.

sections.h2: What are the schools, roads and climate like in North Tonawanda?
sections.html:
The North Tonawanda City School District runs North Tonawanda High School, North Tonawanda Middle School, Drake Elementary, North Tonawanda Intermediate School, Spruce Elementary and Ohio Elementary. The Census Bureau reports that 94.0% of adults 25 and older finished high school and 27.1% hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

Niagara Falls Boulevard, which is US Route 62, marks the northeastern boundary, the Erie Canal runs along the south and much of the east, and Tonawanda Island at the southwest corner belongs to the city. The mean commute is 20.4 minutes. Precipitation falls on about 171 days a year here, and snow on about 57 days, according to NOAA normals reported on Wikipedia, so roof, gutter and basement condition deserve a close look before you list.

faqs.q: Can I sell a rental house in North Tonawanda if it is not registered?
faqs.a: Register it before the sale. Failing to register is a violation with fines of $250 to $500 for a first conviction, and an unpaid fine becomes a lien on the property.

faqs.q: Where do I file a deed after selling in North Tonawanda?
faqs.a: File it with the Niagara County Clerk. The seller pays transfer tax of $2 per $500, and the TP-584 and RP-5217 forms go in with the deed.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in North Tonawanda?
faqs.a: It is always the fourth Tuesday in May. Grievance forms are available from the Assessor's office starting in March.

faqs.q: Is a 14120 mailing address always inside North Tonawanda city limits?
faqs.a: No. The ZIP code 14120 also covers southern parts of the towns of Wheatfield and Pendleton, so check your tax bill to see which municipality governs your house.

faqs.q: What happens to my rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: The certificate lasts up to one year or until ownership changes. After the sale the new owner registers the units with the Building Department.
